page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c6gn.8xlarge in the average performance tier for most multi-core and data-processing workloads. It achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11689.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1894.04 GB/sec and an uncached large block read speed of 181.11 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.34 GB/sec.

The instance is designed for network-intensive, compute-heavy workloads that benefit from ARM64 architecture and high-bandwidth networking. It is well-suited for tasks such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 33.08 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 20432.0 on PassMark database tests and 38.79 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Given its dedicated core allocation and high network throughput without local storage overhead, it offers a resource-dense profile for distributed computing, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation.
